title: Cross-Bad-Case Reviewer Closure Runtime Convergence Benchmark
hypothesis: Reviewer Closure Mode reduces issue churn and extra Review→Repair→Review cycles after a prior semantic blocker is repaired.

design.variant_A: Real qwen reviewer with runtime ReviewerClosureContext deliberately not forwarded.
design.variant_B: Real qwen reviewer with runtime ReviewerClosureContext forwarded normally.
design.evaluable_gate: Both A and B must report a pre-registered PRIMARY_BLOCKER in review round 1, and neither may report a pre-registered CHURN_TRAP in review round 1.
design.confirmed_churn: Only a later review issue matching a pre-registered CHURN_TRAP counts as confirmed churn.

cases.reason: The frozen pre-registered PRIMARY_BLOCKER matcher did not match the round-1 reviewer wording, so the pair is excluded from churn statistics.
Variant A passed the first review and missed the pre-registered primary blocker while variant B detected it; causal comparison is invalid.
Deterministic Verification intercepted the candidate before semantic Reviewer closure conditions were established.

conclusion.reason: Among the five evaluable paired cases, neither baseline nor Closure Mode produced any confirmed churn or extra Review→Repair cycle. With zero discordant pairs, exact paired significance tests are undefined rather than evidence of improvement.
conclusion.overhead_summary: Closure Mode added a mean 723.2 reviewer tokens per evaluable pair, with mean relative overhead 11.60% and median absolute overhead 710 tokens.
conclusion.engineering_interpretation: Closure Mode remains mechanism-valid and caused no observed convergence regression, but this matrix does not justify claiming statistical anti-churn benefit for qwen3.5-flash on these workloads. Do not further tune the Reviewer prompt based on this benchmark alone.
conclusion.next_recommended_phase: Build a broader semantic-pressure challenge set that naturally exhibits fresh-review issue churn across multiple workload shapes before deciding whether Closure Mode should remain unconditional or become risk-triggered.
